Subject: MAP kickoff — cost checks we need before PO

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Our execs liked the latency profile but procurement needs a stronger mutual action plan that includes unit-economics checks before we sign the PO. Specifically they asked for:

- a short evaluation plan (test suite + pass/fail criteria) we can run in the 2-week pilot
- token/$ modeling for our expected workload (chat + embeddings) with caching and batching assumptions called out
- a clear close timeline tied to milestones so we can get finance sign-off

Can you send a draft MAP that includes those items? We are targeting a March 31 commit if the pilot is green — procurement flagged token costs as the main blocker.

Thanks,
Elena

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@fastretail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — cost checks we need before PO

Elena,

Really appreciate the clarity. Attached is a first-pass MAP + cost workbook (redwood_map_v2.pdf, token-econ-sheet.xlsx). High-level notes:

1) Evaluation plan (2-week pilot)
  - Week 1: smoke tests + correctness on 500 prompt samples (pass if >=95% fidelity vs. baseline)
  - Week 2: load ramp to expected QPS for 2m tokens/day across chat + batch embedding jobs
  - Success criteria: latency P95 under 350ms for interactive paths and embedding throughput within 90% of target.

2) Token economics (high level):
  - Baseline assumptions: avg chat prompt+response = 1,200 tokens; embeddings call = 750 tokens (per batch of 32).
  - Expected daily volume: 2,000 interactive reqs + 200 embedding batches → ~2.1M tokens/day.
  - Streaming vs blocking: streaming adds ~5% overhead in token count but reduces user-facing latency.

3) Caching & batching impact (assumptions called out in sheet):
  - Prefix KV caching for common prompts assumed to reduce token generation by 12% on chat path (conservative).
  - Intelligent request-level batching for embeddings reduces per-token execution overhead and improves GPU utilization; modeled at 18% cost reduction from naive approach.
  - Combined effect on model cost: ~27% lower tokens/$ than a no-cache/no-batch baseline in modeled scenario.

4) Proposed milestones / close timeline
  - 03/23: kickoff + test corpus handed off to Redwood
  - 03/24–03/30: pilot run (evaluation + perf)
  - 03/31: decision point — sign PO and enable Dedicated pool if pilot passes

We'll update numbers after you share a sample of your traffic distribution. If procurement needs more granularity I can add per-route cost breakdowns.

Cheers,
Priyom

--
Priyom Das
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
priyom@redwood.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 11:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: MAP kickoff — cost checks we need before PO

Folks — filing a quick internal note before we finalize the sheet for FastRetail. Key open questions I want us to reconcile:

- Are we assuming any quantized model variants for the pilot? That materially affects tokens/$ for generation kernels.
- Do we include fallback to smaller model (cost tiering) in the MAP? Elena's team cares about predictable spend.
- Need a clearer explanation of the cache invalidation policy — they will ask about stale responses.

I'll draft language for the procurement playbook and the SOW addendum. Priyom, can you run the token-econ numbers with a 4-bit quantized model path and add a row for model fallback? Jonas — can you confirm the default batch sizing we will actually enforce for embeddings in Dedicated?

Thanks,
Laura
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 12:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MAP kickoff — cost checks we need before PO

Laura / Priyom — quick answers:

- Quantization: we can run pilot on an int8/4-bit quantized variant for the generation path; in our benchmarks that reduces execution cost per token by ~22% (lower bound) while adding ~6% delta on a small number of edge-case prompts (we'll include quality checks in the eval set).
- Model fallback: absolutely. Proposed MAP language: primary model = q4f (cost-optimized); fallback = fp16 base for safety. Fallback will be triggered by quality thresholds or sustained tail-latency events.
- Embedding batching: for Dedicated we will target batch sizes of 64 in production, but for pilot we recommend 32 to avoid cold-start latency spikes. The sheet models both and shows per-token effective cost at batches 32/64.

I'll attach a short appendix for the cache TTL and invalidation guidance.

—Jonas
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@fastretail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@fastretail.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: MAP + updated token economics for pilot (attached)

Elena — attaching an updated MAP + token-econ-sheet (token-econ-sheet.xlsx) that includes:

- two scenarios: pilot (q4f primary, fallback fp16) and production (q4f + autoscaling + batch 64)
- per-route breakdown: chat interactive, background summarization, embedding batches
- explicit cache assumptions and how token savings are calculated (prefix match % = 12%, TTL 24h)
- simplified cost math: at your current traffic mix we estimate ~0.62 tokens/$ (this is model execution cost only — infra/ops add-ons separate).

Action items for FastRetail: please share a representative 48-hour traffic sample and the 500-sample eval corpus by EOD 03/23 so we can run the pilot with the right distributions. If we get those, we can turn around final PO-ready numbers by 03/30.

Attachments: redwood_map_v2.pdf (MAP draft), token-econ-sheet.xlsx (cost workbook).

Best,
Priyom
From: Elena Morales <elena@fastretail.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@fastretail.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP + updated token economics for pilot (attached)

Priyom,

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail procurement wanted. A couple of quick clarifications before we hand off to our finance team:

1) You mention ~0.62 tokens/$ — can you confirm that is model-exec only (no infra, no storage, no observability)?
2) For the cache savings: is the 12% an optimistic assumption or conservative? We saw 20% in our internal logs for similar prompts.
3) If the pilot moves to Dedicated after PO, will the batching gains (32→64) be automatic or will we need an ops window to change batch configs?

We will send the 48-hour sample tomorrow morning and the eval corpus by EOD. If you can answer the three bullets quickly it will help finance move faster.

—Elena
